content.text:
I rewrote 0.svg into a complete, accessible icon. The sandbox blocked every validation command, so I could not run an XML parser or render the file. The one check that did run was the macOS file-type detector, which identifies the result as an SVG image. I also checked the markup by hand.

The original file was a single empty root element:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>
```

It had no coordinate system, no size, no content, and no accessible name, so it rendered as a blank box at the browser default size.

The new file adds:

- **A viewBox and explicit size** on the standard icon grid, so it scales predictably and has a sensible intrinsic size.
- **An accessible name and description** through a title, a description, and the image role, so screen readers announce it as "Zero".
- **Visible content**, an outlined oval that reads as the digit 0. It is drawn as geometry rather than text, so it does not depend on installed fonts.
- **Stroke color set to currentColor**, so the icon inherits the surrounding text color when inlined and renders black as a standalone image.

One assumption to flag. The original gave no hint of what the image should show, so I drew a "0" based on the filename. If the file is meant to hold different artwork, replace the ellipse element and update the title and description to match.

On the blocked checks: both an XML parser and a QuickLook render required approval that this session cannot grant. I needed them to confirm the markup parses and the glyph looks right. You can run the same checks yourself:

```
xmllint --noout 0.svg
qlmanage -p 0.svg
```
